the prevalence of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations in Mexican women is 5.2% (95% CI 3.7%–6.7%), which is similar to the 5% to 7% prevalence found in the Ashkenazi Jewish population and the 2% to 3% found in the general U.S. population ( 4–6 ).
the BRCA1 mutation is a common mutation in the Mexican population, and it is important to screen for this mutation.
the BRCA 1/2 gene mutations are not the only genetic factors that are responsible for the development of breast cancer in the Mexican population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that BRCA1 and 2 mutations are common in Mexico and that we have identified 22 recurrent mutations in the Mexican population.
we identified 34 Mexican women with breast and/or ovarian cancer with BRCA1/2 mutations.
the BRCA1 gene was found mutated in 11% of Mexican breast cancer patients, while BRCA2 was found mutated in about 4.3% in this population.

the prevalence of mutations is higher than expected.
